ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a regular octagon, with the outer boundary being eight equal-length sides; a set of symmetric diagonals is drawn inside, forming a star-shaped inner boundary; there is a circle in the middle, with the center near the center of the octagon, and the circle is tangent to these internally drawn diagonals. Reasoning: Label the consecutive vertices of the regular octagon clockwise as A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H, and let the center be O. Take one representative tangent diagonal AD in the figure, which connects vertices separated by three vertices. The central angle corresponding to adjacent vertices of a regular octagon is 360°/8=45°, so ∠AOD=3×45°=135°. Let M be the midpoint of chord AD, then OM is perpendicular to AD; because the circle is tangent to AD, the radius of the circle is OM. If the circumradius is R, then side length AB=2R sin(45°/2)=2R sin22.5°. Given AB=10, so R sin22.5°=5. Also OM=R cos(135°/2)=R cos67.5°=R sin22.5°, therefore OM=5. Thus the radius of the required circle is 5.

method.method_draft: Describe the diagram as a regular octagon with a symmetric set of drawn diagonals forming a star-like inner boundary; the circle is centered at the octagon center and tangent to one representative drawn diagonal. Label consecutive vertices A,B,C,D,... and use the image to pick a tangent diagonal such as AD, which joins vertices three steps apart. Since the octagon is regular, the central angle between adjacent vertices is 45°, so ∠AOD = 135°. If M is the midpoint of chord AD, then OM is perpendicular to AD and equals the desired radius. Use the side length AB = 10 to get the circumradius from AB = 2R sin 22.5°. Then compute OM = R cos 67.5° = R sin 22.5° = 10/2 = 5.
